Careers and Work Related Learning
Students are offered a structured programme of careers and work related learning events to support them to progress after leaving Wheatley Park.
Our programme includes:
Career Stereotypes in Year 7
Enterprise Challenge in Year 8
OXLEP Careers Fest and Take Your Child to Work Day in Year 9
Post 16 Options activities and work experience in Year 10
Making applications in Year 11
Professional practice week in Year 12
Morrisby Profile testing in Year 12
UCAS applications in Year 13
Apprenticeship and employment support in Year 11 and Year 13
One to one personalised careers meetings with a qualified independent careers adviser for all Year 11 students and those in any year group on request.
Students have access to a range of careers resources in the Careers Hub in the school library and via a dedicated careers website on the student portal. All students have a Morrisby Careers account and access to many other resources including EClips and the National Careers Service.
We work with a range of partners to deliver our programme including Adviza, Activate Learning (City of Oxford College), Abingdon and Witney College, training providers, universities, volunteers from the business community and the Local Enterprise Partnership (LEP). We work closely with our Enterprise Co-ordinator and Enterprise Adviser to achieve the Gatsby Benchmarks.
Our programme is reviewed on an ongoing basis with a formal annual review at the end of the academic year. This includes student and tutor surveys and feedback.
The careers team is:
Our Careers Lead and Adviser is Alison Bennett.
Our senior leadership team link is Katie Clifton Rabone who can be contacted at kclifton@wheatleypark.org.
Our Careers Administrator is Val Wolstenholme.
If you would like to contact us to find out more about our careers provision, you can contact us by emailing careers@wheatleypark.org or calling the main school switchboard on 01865 872441.
If you are enquiring about employment with Wheatley Park School please see our vacancy page.

Parents and Carers
Careers guidance
We are keen to involve parents and carers in the preparation of our students leaving school at the end of Year 11 or Year 13.
Personalised one to one careers meetings with a qualified independent careers adviser are available for all Year 11 students, and those in any year group on request.
The careers adviser attends relevant parents' evenings including Year 8 Guided Choices, Year 11 and the Post 16 open evening. Parents and Carers can also request meetings at other times to suit them.
If you would like to arrange a time to speak with the careers adviser please email us at abennett@wheatleypark.org
Choices after Year 11
Every young person needs to stay in education until they are 18. This can be in the sixth form, at college, an apprenticeship, a traineeship or in a job with approved training.
Your son or daughter will be introduced to the options in Year 10 where they will have an opportunity to meet with different colleges and apprenticeship providers, as well as the Sixth Form. In Year 11 they will make their applications to their preferred institutions, focussing on applications to the Sixth Form and colleges in the Autumn Term and to apprenticeships in the Spring Term. All students are expected to have a Plan A and Plan B in place before they leave school.

Headteacher's Welcome
A warm welcome to Wheatley Park School, a thriving and inclusive 11 - 18 academy within the River Learning Trust set in stunning parkland five miles east of Oxford.
At Wheatley Park, we are committed to our twin values: Everyone Learning and Everyone Caring.
We believe highly effective learning is rooted in the highest quality care.
So, first and foremost we care for the health, safety and wellbeing of each member of our vibrantly diverse community. We care about making a positive difference to those around us and in the wider world. And we care about nurturing the strong relationships between all our stakeholders that underpin our ongoing success.
Our climate of care enables everyone to flourish as learners. Our students are learning to be powerful learners, equipped to achieve excellence at school and to relish the lifetime of learning that will follow. Our teachers are learning to be ever better teachers who challenge, inspire and enrich students both in the classroom and beyond. And our leaders are learning to be ever better leaders, striving to optimise every aspect of the student experience.
Thank you for taking an interest in our school. Please do not hesitate to contact us for further information or to arrange a visit. I look forward to welcoming you to our beautiful historic site.
Tim Martin Headteacher

Exam Results
Wheatley Park School GCSE Results 2026
Congratulations to the Class of 2026 for comprehensively smashing school records with their GCSE results!
This year’s ‘Attainment 8’ score (a key government measurement of overall GCSE performance) of 56.5 is a significant advance on the previous best of 53.9, with students from disadvantaged backgrounds in particular achieving more highly than ever before.
39% of all GCSEs were awarded at Grade 7 (equivalent to an old ‘A’ grade) or above, with 44% of students achieving a Grade 7 or above in either English Language or English Literature and 33% achieving a Grade 7 or above in maths.
This cohort missed their Year 6 SATs due to the pandemic, but based on nationally standardised English and maths tests that they completed at the beginning of Year 7, we calculate that their record breaking attainment has been matched by record breaking progress.
Amongst countless stories of individual triumph, special mention must go to Amelie Livesey who achieved straight Grade 9s.
Otis and Eva Nightall were one of several sets of successful twin siblings, achieving four Grade 9s apiece.
We are incredibly proud of each and every member of the Class of 2026.
By thoroughly embracing our school value of Everyone Caring, they created such a supportive year group culture that their success in demonstrating our other school value of Everyone Learning is no surprise.
Whether they are staying on at our Sixth Form or continuing to college or apprenticeships, we wish our Wheatley Parkers every success - may your blood continue to run purple!
Neirin Wheeler, Head of Year 11
Tim Martin, Headteacher
Amelie Livesey achieved straight Grade 9s
Twins, Otis and Eva Nightall achieved four Grade 9s apiece
Wheatley Park Post-16 Results 2026
Massive congratulations to our Year 12 and 13 students on their brilliant A-level, AS-level and BTEC examination results.
At A-level, our biggest ever cohort of 117 students has achieved the strongest results since 2022 (when grades were awarded more generously after the pandemic). 28% of grades gained were awarded at A* or A, 59% at A* to B, 85% at A* to C and 100% at A* to E.
A special mention must go to Imogen Flight who has maintained a perfect academic record, following up her twelve A*s at GCSE with four A*s at A-level in computer science, history, maths and further maths.
Meanwhile, Amir Shodunke demonstrated an incredible work ethic to gain A grades in five subjects (chemistry, computer science, maths, further maths and physics) and complete an Extended Project Qualification into the bargain, for which he engineered a litter-picking robot!
Most importantly, the vast majority of students gained the grades needed to access their next steps on university degrees, degree apprenticeships, apprenticeships or in employment.
Thank you to all our Year 13s for being fully ‘purple-blooded’ Wheatley Parkers who have role-modelled our school values of Everyone Learning and Everyone Caring at every opportunity - all the very best for the future.
Finally, an enormous thank you and a fond farewell to our much-loved and highly-respected Head of Sixth Form, Graham West, who retires this summer after leading our Sixth Form so successfully for the last nine years of his twenty-five years at WPS and thirty years in teaching.
Tim Martin, Headteacher
Imogen Flight, with her mother, achieved 4 A*s at A-level following on from 12 A*s at GCSE
Amir Shodunke achieved A grades in 5 A-levels.
Mr West retires after 9 years as Head of Sixth Form and 25 years at Wheatley Park School.

Chromebook Options
A Chromebook for every Student - Select your Chromebook option
If you are the guardian of a student currently in Year 7 (or another year group and would like to change your option) please select one of the options below to inform us of your preferred choice and make any payment required:
Purchase - Single Payment
£232 - Please contact [email protected] to arrange a payment on MCAS.
Purchase - Monthly payments (12 months)
Monthly Payments (12 months) Visit the Edde Portal and pick the 12 month option - Use Code WPS28-28.
Purchase - Monthly payments (24 months)
Monthly Payments (24 months) Visit the Edde Portal and pick the 24 month option - Use Code WPS28-28.
Chromebook Loan Agreement Form (Required for Loan in addition to payment via MCAS)
£100 - Please contact [email protected] to arrange a payment on MCAS.
School day only loan
No payment required. Please complete the Day Loan request form.
Bring my own Chromebook
No payment required. Please complete the Own Chromebook form.
For further information on each option please see page 5 of the Parents’ Information Booklet.
Payments
For more information please see here:
June 2026 Letter
June 2026 Parents Guide
Support and Assistance
If you would like to discuss any of the options above or assistance with making payments please contact us via [email protected]
Warranty
All purchased Chromebooks come with a 3 year manufacturer’s warranty and in the event of the device malfunctioning, we will return the Chromebook to the manufacturer on your behalf and issue a replacement device until the original is returned.
We will carry out repairs at the cost of any parts required. Optionally, you can add the Chromebook to your home insurance or purchase separate gadget insurance.
Accidental damage costs (please note that these are estimates and prices vary):
Please be advised that parents will need to pay for repairs even in the case of deliberate damage by other students. Where such damage is provable, the school may request a contribution from the parents of the responsible party but cannot enforce this. Parents should take this into account when considering their insurance options.
